verdict: Microsoft grew 18% to $62.0B as Azure jumped 30% and Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $33.7B — and it kept $21.9B as profit, about 35 cents of every dollar, in its first quarter with Activision Blizzard on board.

segments.name: Productivity and Business Processes
segments.note: Office 365, LinkedIn and Dynamics — Office Commercial cloud services grew 15%, LinkedIn 9% and Dynamics 365 27%.

segments.name: Intelligent Cloud
segments.note: Azure and server products — Azure and other cloud services grew 30% as AI demand added to regular cloud growth.

segments.name: More Personal Computing
segments.note: Windows, Xbox and search ads — Xbox content and services up 61% with Activision Blizzard included for the first time; Windows up 9%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Spending on building products, led by AI and cloud — up 4% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling and marketing the product line — up 10% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — down 15% YoY.

follow100Note: The rows reconcile to the $35.26 kept as profit within $0.01 of rounding; other expense is a $0.82 drag per $100 of revenue.
footerNote: Segments use Microsoft's FY24 reporting structure (three segments, as reported at the time).

takeaways.title: Azure sped up
takeaways.text: Azure and other cloud services grew 30% — faster than the quarter before — as AI demand added to regular cloud growth; Microsoft Cloud overall reached $33.7B, up 24%.

takeaways.title: The first Activision quarter
takeaways.text: The quarter included Activision Blizzard for the first time (the deal closed October 13, 2023): Xbox content and services revenue jumped 61%, with 55 points of that growth coming from the acquisition.

takeaways.title: A third of sales became profit
takeaways.text: Net income rose 33% to $21.9B — about 35 cents of every revenue dollar — even as Microsoft kept spending heavily on the data centers behind its AI push.
